introduction: On this Sunday, Solomon prays that God will hear the prayers of foreigners who come to his temple. In the Gospel, a Roman centurion asks Jesus to heal his servant, saying, Lord, I am not worthy for you to come under my roof; but say the word, and my servant will be healed. Jesus marvels at his faith. Paul warns the Galatians not to desert the Gospel. Let us come to Jesus with the humble faith of the centurion.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord's faithfulness endures forever. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may faithfully hand on the Gospel she has received. Let us pray to the Lord.
For people of every nation who seek God: that they may find him and be welcomed. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the sick and those who care for them: that they may trust in the healing word of Jesus. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those in positions of authority: that they may care for those who serve under them, as the centurion cared for his servant. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may approach Communion with humility and great faith. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, your Son marveled at the faith of the centurion. Give us his humility and trust, so that we may receive your word and be healed. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Say the word
reflection.body:
At the dedication of the temple in Jerusalem, Solomon prays not only for Israel but also for foreigners: "concerning the foreigner, who is not of your people Israel, when he comes out of a far country for your name's sake." He asks God to hear their prayers, "that all the peoples of the earth may know your name." The psalm echoes this: "Praise the LORD, all you nations!"

In the Gospel, we meet such a foreigner. A Roman centurion, an officer of the occupying army, has a servant "who was dear to him" who is close to death. He sends Jewish elders to ask Jesus for help, and they speak well of him: "he loves our nation, and he built our synagogue for us."

As Jesus approaches the house, the centurion sends friends with a remarkable message: "Lord, don't trouble yourself, for I am not worthy for you to come under my roof." He believes Jesus does not even need to come: "but say the word, and my servant will be healed." As a soldier, he understands authority: when he gives an order, it is carried out. He believes that Jesus' word has that kind of power over sickness.

Jesus is amazed: "I tell you, I have not found such great faith, no, not in Israel." And the servant is healed.

The Church has made the centurion's words her own. Just before Communion, at every Mass, we echo his humble faith, acknowledging that we are not worthy to receive the Lord, yet trusting that his word can heal us.

Paul warns the Galatians not to desert the Gospel for a different message: there is no other gospel. The faith we have received is a precious gift to be kept faithfully.

This week, when you prepare for Communion, pray the centurion's words slowly and mean them. And pray for someone who is sick, trusting in the power of Jesus' word.
